script.title: Sunlight, Sorted by Color: Why Is the Sky Blue?

voice_performance.performance_intent: Warm, curious science narrator: unhurried, a friend pointing at the sky.
voice_performance.energy_curve: Curious hook -> steady build -> playful twist -> slow, calm landing
voice_performance.pause_policy: Short pause after each section; longer pause before the final three short sentences.

provider_notes.piper: No emotion controls: rely on punctuation, per-section synthesis, length_scale tuned so total narration lands near 43s, and inserted silences between sections.

sections.label: Hook
sections.text: Sunlight is white. Space is black. So why is the sky blue?
sections.speaker_directions: measured pace, curious; emphasize white, black, blue. Three short beats; slight lift on the question.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: Three short beats; slight lift on the question.
delivery_cues.provider_text: Sunlight is white. Space is black. So why is the sky blue?

enhancement_cues.description: Black space, a white Sun; a white beam travels toward a small Earth; the sky over Earth glows blue as the question lands

sections.label: White light is every color
sections.text: That white light is really every color mixed together, each one a wave of a different length.
sections.speaker_directions: conversational pace, warm; emphasize every, length. Unfold the idea gently.

delivery_cues.provider_text: That white light is really every color mixed together, each one a wave of a different length.

enhancement_cues.description: The white beam fans out into six colored sine waves; red long and lazy, violet short and tight

sections.label: Molecules are picky
sections.text: When sunlight hits our air, tiny nitrogen and oxygen molecules scatter it. But they're picky: short blue waves scatter about five times more than long red ones.
sections.speaker_directions: measured pace, intrigued; emphasize picky, five times. Pause after 'picky' to set up the reveal.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: Pause after 'picky' to set up the reveal.
delivery_cues.provider_text: When sunlight hits our air, tiny nitrogen and oxygen molecules scatter it. But they're picky: short blue waves scatter about five times more than long red ones.

enhancement_cues.description: Zoom to molecule scale: N2/O2 dots; a red wave passes straight through, a blue wave hits a molecule and splashes outward

sections.label: Blue from everywhere
sections.text: So blue gets bounced all across the sky, and reaches your eyes from every direction.
sections.speaker_directions: conversational pace, satisfied; emphasize every direction. Land the payoff, slightly brighter.

delivery_cues.provider_text: So blue gets bounced all across the sky, and reaches your eyes from every direction.

enhancement_cues.description: Pull back: blue waves ricochet between molecules, filling the sky; a little person looks up, blue arrows arrive from all around

sections.label: Why not violet?
sections.text: Violet is even shorter, so why not a purple sky? The Sun sends less violet, and your eyes are tuned to blue.
sections.speaker_directions: measured pace, playful; emphasize even shorter, tuned to blue. Pose the question with a smile, then answer plainly.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: Pose the question with a smile, then answer plainly.
delivery_cues.provider_text: Violet is even shorter, so why not a purple sky? The Sun sends less violet, and your eyes are tuned to blue.

enhancement_cues.description: The sky briefly tints violet with a question mark; sunlight spectrum bars show less violet; an eye icon with a sensitivity curve peaking toward blue/green; the sky settles back to blue

sections.label: Sunset and landing
sections.text: At sunset, light crosses so much air that the blue is scattered away, leaving reds and oranges. Same air. Same physics. Just sunlight, sorted by color.
sections.speaker_directions: slow pace, calm wonder; emphasize sunset, sorted by color. Slow down for the final three short sentences.

delivery_cues.delivery_note: Slow down for the final three short sentences.
delivery_cues.provider_text: At sunset, light crosses so much air that the blue is scattered away, leaving reds and oranges. Same air. Same physics. Just sunlight, sorted by color.

enhancement_cues.description: Sun sinks to the horizon; its beam crosses a long slab of air; blue peels off along the way and only red/orange arrive; sky turns amber
